title: Infra GPU Fleet, Capacity, Cloud Accounts & Networking, IaC Modules, CI/CD Playbook (Comprehensive)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook consolidates our infrastructure engineering standards and runbooks for GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD build pipelines. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for provisioning, scaling, and operating Redwood's inference-serving infrastructure.

Scope
-----
- GPU fleet sizing, autoscaling, and cost controls
- Cloud accounts, VPC topology, peering, and transit networking
- Terraform modules, registry, and module lifecycle
- CI/CD pipelines for infra modules and GPU-serving services
- Runbooks for capacity events, incident triage, and change rollouts

Owners and Contacts
-------------------
- Primary owner: infra-engineering (on-call: infra-oncall@redwood.example.com)
- Capacity lead: Priya Shah (priya@redwood.example.com)
- Cloud accounts & networking: Diego Morales (diego@redwood.example.com)
- IaC/CI-CD owner: Evan Liu (evan@redwood.example.com)

Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Targets
------------------------------------------
- API serving P95 latency (model inference): <= 250ms (hosted)
- GPU allocation request latency (time to provision node in pool): <= 5 minutes for warm pools, <= 30 minutes for cold scale-up
- Autoscaler correctness: >= 99% of scale decisions succeed without operator intervention
- Capacity buffer target: maintain 15% spare GPU capacity in each region and zone during business hours

High-level Architecture (text diagram)
------------------------------------
- Control Plane (Redwood control plane) -> Orchestrates model routing, placement, and deployment state
- GPU Serving Plane (region-specific):
  - GPU node pools (warm/cold tiers)
  - Load balancers (L4 LB per pool)
  - Cache layer (KV cache instances)
  - Metrics and tracing collectors
- Networking: VPC per-account, inter-region transit peering (where applicable), centralized egress NAT

GPU Fleet & Capacity Guidelines
------------------------------
1. Node types and sizing
   - Preferred instance types: A100-80GB, A10G (for cost-tier), H100 (for high throughput)
   - Warm pools: provisioned with preloaded container images and warmed kernel caches; target startup time < 2m
   - Cold pools: scale based on predicted demand and spot capacity; acceptable startup time <= 30m

2. Pool tiers
   - Dedicated-critical (reserved capacity for enterprise customers) \u2014 SLA-backed, pinned models
   - Production (general-purpose) \u2014 autoscaled, priority scheduling
   - Spot-economy (best-effort) \u2014 used for non-SLA workloads and overflow

3. Capacity planning process (quarterly)
   - Inputs: traffic growth forecasts, model footprint matrix (tokens/sec per model), historical utilization by hour
   - Output: target capacity by region, pool-level reserve (15%) and purchase plan (commit vs spot)
   - Approval: Capacity plan reviewed by infra execs and finance before procurement

4. Autoscaling behavior
   - Horizontal scaling for model pods where supported; fall back to vertical scaling for stateful KV-heavy services
   - Scale-up triggers: sustained > 70% GPU utilization for 3 minutes or queued work > threshold
   - Scale-down policy: cooldown 10 minutes, minimum pool size maintained (as per pool tier)

5. Cost controls
   - Tagging policy: cost-center, team, environment, model-owner \u2014 enforced at provisioning
   - Bounded overprovisioning: automated daily reclaim job that reports and reclaims idle capacity > 12h

Cloud Accounts & Networking Standards
------------------------------------
- Account layout
  - Per-environment accounts (prod-us-west-2, prod-eu-west-1, staging-*, dev-*)
  - Shared services account for logging, CI artifacts, and central observability

- VPC & Subnet topology
  - VPC per account, multi-AZ subnets (public for LB, private for workloads)
  - Dedicated subnets for GPU pools with strict egress controls
  - Route tables: explicit routes for peered VPCs and transit gateways

- Security groups / firewall rules
  - Minimum required ingress: LB -> pool on ports 443 and gRPC ports (as defined per-service)
  - Outbound: restricted to telemetry endpoints, model registry, artifact repositories
  - Management plane (SSH/remote) blocked from internet; access via bastion/SSO only

- IAM & service accounts
  - Principle of least privilege: roles scoped to account & resource namespace
  - Long-lived credentials are prohibited; use short-lived STS tokens and KMS-integrated keys

IaC (Terraform) Module Standards
--------------------------------
- Module registry location: internal Terraform Registry (registry.redwood.internal)
- Naming conventions: module_gpu_pool, module_vpc_network, module_iam_role, module_lb_frontend
- Module structure requirements:
  - README.md with inputs/outputs and example usage
  - documented state migration notes in changelog
  - semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; breaking changes require MAJOR bump and ADR

- Example module usage (terraform snippet)
  ```terraform
  module "gpu_pool_production" {
    source = "registry.redwood.internal/modules/gpu_pool"
    version = "1.4.0"

    region           = "us-west-2"
    instance_type    = "a100-80gb"
    min_size         = 4
    max_size         = 200
    pool_tier        = "production"
    node_image       = "gcr.io/redwood/gpu-runtime:2026-01-10"
    prewarm_enabled  = true
  }
  ```

- State management
  - Remote state in encrypted bucket with state-locking (DynamoDB for AWS)
  - Per-account state workspace, automated backups and drift detection weekly

CI/CD and Build Practices (Infra Modules + Serving Services)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Pipeline layout
  - PR Validation: terraform fmt, terraform validate, unit tests (kitchen/terratest), linting
  - Merge Gate: automated plan + human approval for any plan that changes production resources
  - Release: tag-based releases that publish module to internal registry and create release notes
  - Canary: staged rollout for infra changes impacting production pools with smoke checks

- Recommended GitHub Actions workflow (high level)
  - on: pull_request -> run: fmt, validate, terratest
  - on: push ./releases -> run: publish module, bump registry, notify mod-dev channel

- Artifact storage
  - Build artifacts (container images) pushed to internal registry (gcr.io/redwood) with immutability policy
  - Module packages stored in internal Terraform registry with retention and immutability for released versions

Testing and Validation
----------------------
- Unit: terratest or local terraform plan comparison against canonical fixtures
- Integration: create ephemeral account/workspace using CI runner, apply module, run smoke tests (node joins pool, LB health checks pass)
- Chaos: scheduled game-days that test node failures, preemptions, and capacity reclaim behavior

Runbooks (Operational Procedures)
--------------------------------
1) Capacity shortage (high-level)
   - Detection: Alert "GPU Pool Utilization > 90% (5m avg)" fires in PagerDuty
   - Immediate action (on-call):
     1. Verify global dashboard for impacted region and identify which pools are saturated
     2. Check autoscaler logs: /observability/autoscaler/{region} for recent failures
     3. If autoscaler healthy but demand high: increase pool max_size via emergency Terraform variable override (see emergency flags)
     4. If autoscaler failing: escalate to infra-engineering with logs and diagnostics bundle (run /scripts/collect-capacity-bundle.sh)
     5. Notify product & customer-success if enterprise customers are impacted
   - Postmortem: within 48 hours, create incident doc and capacity mitigation plan

2) Adding warm capacity (planned)
   - Preflight checklist:
     - Confirm image versions and node images are in registry
     - Confirm IAM role and permissions exist for new nodes
     - Validate Terraform plan in staging workspace and run integration tests
   - Rollout steps:
     1. Open PR to update module inputs (min_size / prewarm_enabled)
     2. Run pipeline and approve plan after review
     3. Apply during maintenance window or low-traffic period
     4. Monitor allocation, health checks, and cost dashboards for 2 hours

3) Evicting idle capacity / reclaiming
   - Run reclaim report: /infra/scripts/reclaim-idle.sh --hours=12 --dry-run
   - Validate owners listed by tag; notify owners 48 hours before reclaim
   - Apply reclamation via terraform workspace targeting affected pools

Change Management and Safe Deployments
-------------------------------------
- All production-impacting terraform plans require at least one approver and a three-hour review window
- Canary rollout: 10% of nodes roll, validate 15m of telemetry, increase to 50% if healthy, then full rollout
- Rollback: Terraform can be used to revert inputs; for image-level rollbacks use container registry tag rollback and force a restart on nodes

Diagnostics and Observability
----------------------------
- Metrics to surface on capacity dashboard:
  - GPU utilization (1m/5m/15m) per pool
  - Queue length / pending inference requests
  - Node startup time distribution (median, P95)
  - Autoscaler decision latency and errors
- Logs: centralized ELK/CloudWatch; ensure correlation IDs are propagated from front door through runtime
- Traces: sample 1% of inference requests, increase during canary to 100% for affected models

Oncall Playbook (Short)
----------------------
- PagerDuty triage steps:
  1. Acknowledge alert, create incident in incident tracker
  2. Look up recent deploys (last 60 minutes) and Terraform plans affecting pools
  3. Run diagnostics script: /scripts/infra-diagnostics.sh {region} > /tmp/diag.json and upload to incident doc
  4. If escalation required, page infra lead and capacity lead

Runbook Appendices
------------------
- Useful commands:
  - terraform workspace select prod-us-west-2
  - terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars
  - aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:pool,Values=gpu-production"

- Example smoke test (bash)
  ```bash
  # verify new node joins pool and becomes healthy
  ./ci/smoke-check-node-join.sh --region us-west-2 --pool production
  ```

Onboarding and Team Wiki Guidance
--------------------------------
- New infra hires should complete the following within 30 days:
  1. Read this playbook and related IaC module READMEs
  2. Run the local terratest suite and create a sandbox workspace
  3. Shadow oncall for two rotations and attend a game-day
  4. Complete security checklist with Diego (networking) and KMS onboarding with Security team

Document Maintenance
--------------------
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly by the infra steering committee. Major changes (networking topology, purchasing commitments, or SLO changes) must go through an ADR and be noted in the changelog.
